title: Starship
tagline: The biggest rocket ever flown. Spin it, launch it, catch it.
dadNotes: Height: about 124 m for the version flying now. Big Ben's tower is 96 m, so Starship is about a quarter taller.
Booster (Super Heavy) is about 72 m tall with 33 Raptor engines. The Ship on top is about 52 m with 6 engines: 3 for air, 3 big-belled ones for space.
Fuel: liquid methane and liquid oxygen, kept super cold. Liquid oxygen is about minus 183 °C.
It's made of stainless steel: cheap, strong when super cold, and copes with heat better than carbon fibre.
About 18,000 black heat-shield tiles protect the Ship at about 1,400 °C when it comes back from space.
First booster catch: Flight 5, 13 October 2024. Boosters have been caught three times (Flights 5, 7 and 8).
First time in orbit: Flight 14, 28 September 2026, with 26 Starlink satellites. Nobody has caught the Ship yet; SpaceX may try on Flight 15, possibly later this month.
Plans: an uncrewed Moon landing as early as 2027. Mars has been put on the back burner for now.

steps.title: Meet Starship
steps.text: This is Starship, the biggest rocket ever built. It's made of shiny steel, like a giant saucepan.
steps.wow: 124 metres tall: taller than Big Ben!
steps.dad: Ask: what do you think a rocket this big is for?

steps.title: Explore Starship
steps.intro: Spin it with your finger. Tap the glowing dots. Try Cutaway to see inside, then press LAUNCH!

hotspots.title: 33 engines
hotspots.text: The booster has 33 Raptor engines. They all light up at once with a giant roar.
hotspots.wow: More engines than any rocket ever!

hotspots.title: Ship engines
hotspots.text: The ship has 6 engines. 3 small ones work best in air. 3 big ones work best in space.

hotspots.title: Grid fins
hotspots.text: These metal waffles steer the booster as it falls back home. The tower catches it just below them.

hotspots.title: Hot-staging ring
hotspots.text: The ship lights its engines while it's still sitting on the booster. The fire escapes through these holes.
hotspots.wow: It lights up before it lets go!

hotspots.title: Oxygen tank
hotspots.text: The biggest tank holds liquid oxygen. Fire needs oxygen, and there's none in space, so the rocket brings its own.
hotspots.wow: Colder than the coldest place on Earth!

hotspots.title: Methane tank
hotspots.text: This tank holds liquid methane, the fuel. Methane and oxygen burn together to make the fire.
hotspots.wow: One day we might make methane on Mars!

hotspots.title: Ship's tanks
hotspots.text: The ship has its own fuel tanks, so it can keep flying after the booster lets go.
hotspots.wow: About 1,600 tonnes of fuel: as heavy as 1,000 cars!

hotspots.title: Header tanks
hotspots.text: Little tanks in the nose keep some fuel safe and ready for landing.

hotspots.title: Cargo bay
hotspots.text: This is the space for cargo. Today it carries satellites. One day it could carry astronauts.
hotspots.wow: 100 tonnes: as heavy as a blue whale!

hotspots.title: Flaps
hotspots.text: Four flaps steer the ship as it falls back from space, like a skydiver using arms and legs.

hotspots.title: Heat shield
hotspots.text: About 18,000 black tiles stop the ship getting too hot when it comes back from space.

hotspots.title: The catching tower
hotspots.text: The launch tower has two giant arms called chopsticks. They catch the booster in mid-air!
hotspots.wow: One and a half Big Bens tall!

launchBeats.caption: Liftoff! Starship climbs past the tower.
Max-Q: the air is pushing hardest now. Hold on!
Hot staging! The ship lights its engines and lets go.
The booster flips round and heads back home.
The ship is in space. Look at the curve of the Earth!
Coming home belly first, glowing like a shooting star.
Flip, engines on... and a soft landing!

steps.title: Guess!
steps.prompt: How many engines does the booster have?
steps.reveal: 33 engines! More than any rocket ever. They all light up together at liftoff.

steps.title: Two rockets in one
steps.text: Starship has two parts. The giant booster at the bottom lifts everything off the ground. Then the ship on top flies on into space by itself.
steps.wow: The booster alone is as tall as 60 Finns standing on each other's heads!
steps.dad: Point at the 3D model: which part is the booster, and which is the ship?

steps.title: Guess!
steps.prompt: Which is taller: Starship or Big Ben?
steps.reveal: Starship! It's about 124 metres tall. Big Ben's tower is 96 metres. Starship would peek over the top.

steps.title: Rockets that come home
steps.text: Most rockets are used once and thrown away. Starship's booster flies back home, and the tower catches it with giant arms called chopsticks.
steps.dad: Ask: why is it better to catch a rocket than throw it away?

steps.title: The very first catch
steps.why: 13 October 2024. Watch the booster come back and the tower's arms close around it.

steps.title: Catch the Booster
steps.intro: Hold THRUST to slow down. Steer left and right. Land between the arms, nice and slow!

steps.title: Big Question: The Catch
steps.scenario: It's October 2024. The giant booster is falling back towards your only tower. If the catch goes wrong, the tower could break, and you couldn't launch for a long time.

options.label: Try to catch it!
options.detail: Exciting, and we'd learn how to reuse rockets.

options.label: Land it in the sea
options.detail: The tower stays safe, but the booster is lost.

options.label: Only catch it if everything is perfect
options.detail: Check every engine first. If anything's wrong, go to the sea.

steps.reveal: SpaceX chose something like the last one. The booster checked itself all the way down. Everything looked good, and the tower caught it on the very first try! On another flight, something wasn't quite right, so they sent it to the sea instead.
steps.followUp: Is checking first brave, or careful? Can it be both?

steps.title: Falling like a skydiver
steps.text: Coming back from space, the ship falls belly first, like a skydiver. Black tiles stop it getting too hot. Right at the end, it flips upright and lights its engines to land.
steps.wow: About 18,000 tiles: more than the bricks in a big house!
steps.dad: Try it: lie flat on the floor like the ship, then flip up onto your feet!

steps.title: Starship news
steps.text: Just last month, on 28 September 2026, Starship flew all the way around the Earth for the first time. Next, SpaceX wants to try catching the ship too. Nobody has ever done that!
steps.wow: Next stop: the Moon, maybe in 2027
steps.dad: Flight 15 might try the first ship catch soon. Check the news together!

steps.title: Try it at home: Balloon rocket
need: A long piece of string (about 4 metres)
steps: Thread the string through the straw.
Tie the string tight between two chairs.
Blow up the balloon, but don't tie it. Pinch the end shut.
Tape the balloon under the straw, with the end pointing backwards.
Count down from 10... and let go!
Try again with more air, or less. Which goes further?
steps.why: Air rushes out of the back and pushes the balloon forwards. Starship's engines do the same thing, with fire instead of air!

debrief: Why do you think SpaceX wants to catch rockets instead of throwing them away?
